reviews.title: SCAM! Refuse to respond or cancel my subscription
reviews.text: I have no problem with there actually content, I enjoyed it when I used it. I signed up through Apple. I canceled but noticed I was still being charged on my bank statement. I double checked that my subscription through Apple was canceled. It was. I reached out to customer service and they responded immediately. They asked for screenshots and some other basic information. Somehow another account with my card was opened through there site. We talked back and forth a few times and the second I gave them my information they stopped responding. I cannot get them to respond and they are still charging me $8 a week! It’s been over 20 days since they responded. DO NOT TRUST THEM

Every time I wait the amount of time until I can read the next chapter and I go to click on the book it uses it for the same chapter I am already on then wants me to wait another amount of time. I have been stuck on the same chapters for the last week. I honestly don’t wanna bother so I’m deleting it but just so everyone knows.

reviews.title: Basic & Overpriced
reviews.text:
Stories are very basic and run of the mill - they’re okay to read, but something you could find written better on multiple different platforms. This alone isn’t worth a 2 star rating, I would have put it at four if it weren’t for their pricing model.

The fact that there is not an option to do a monthly subscription and you are forced into the $70 one right off the bad is ridiculous. Points are useless, to buy enough points to read an entire book would be more than the unlimited access cost. The point cost to immediately read more chapters towards the beginning of the books are only 10, and increase the further into the book you get. So if you buy 110 points thinking you’ll get 11 chapters out of your $8 spent, you’re wrong. They use a similar pay model to webtoon apps, which work because they are visual mediums with slow updates. This doesn’t work on a novel app, when chapters are short enough to be read in less than two minutes.

I am a firm believer that authors should be paid fairly for their work, but the model Galatea uses is unfair to the reader, and not worth the money. The chapters are, as mentioned before, incredibly short. The chapters unlock for free in six hours, but even if you manage to hit all four of the times a chapter is free for you in a 24 hour time period you aren’t getting as much content as you would expect out of even a singular chapter. I’d be more than willing to spend money on one book at a time, but that is not an option either. Avoid Galatea and

reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.text:
An ad popped up with the first Chapter of a story, which although not brilliant writing, was engaging enough to download the app.
I am very happy to pay a monthly subscription to read a series but do dislike being required to pay for an annual sub.  The alternative is a drip feed of free chapters. Each “chapter” is incredibly short and generally seems to take six hours to be released on the “free” plan.  I gather from reviews there used to be advertising to allow chapter release but this has been dropped, which is a shame as it seems that would benefit both authors and readers.
I’ll probably persevere until the initial book is finished but may equally simply drop it, if the plot doesn’t pick up.  
In all a very disappointing app which could probably be a lot more user friendly and thus more profitable for the self published authors it represents

reviews.title: Need Better Point System
reviews.text:
Just download the app because I was interested in a couple of stories and it sparked my interest into actually reading again instead of just audiobooks.  However…  I would definitely rate higher if…  1.) Had a better “free” point system to earn points instead of “1 point/coin” daily for completing ONE Chapter (and the cost for each chapter increases as you move forward.)   2.) It’s a bit pricey for subscription in my opinion of course because there are only a couple-few books I have time to read.  In my opinion if they actually physically sold a paperback book of the story I wouldn’t mind spending $10-$15 on the book(s) versus a $70-$100 billed annually or .
The reason why I say this is because I’d rather complete one story rather than having to jump into another story while I wait until I accumulate enough points/coins for the next chapter of a book I’m genuinely interested in.  So me of us don’t have the luxury or paying $4 for 40 Points up to $25 for 550 Points for Chapter(s). Again, as you move forward with each chapter of the story the points increase to continue costing more than a physical hardcover book. Some do NOT have that kind of luxury fund to enjoy reading a complete story here and there or every now and then.  But if you’re an avid reader and have the means to do so by all means spend the money. reviews.title: Be forewarned.
reviews.text: So. Nice app on the surface of things, works fantastically. But it’s a bit of a scam, spending on what you want to do and how you want to read. You get about 11 free points to begin with. A book maybe has 55 chapters or more. And you don’t know if that’s just book 1 of 3, or a book all its own. Each chapter begins costing you about 4 points. Sounds ok, right? Doable? Affordable? 4 points per chapter, 55 chapters; it’ll cost you 220points. Or so you think. You decide hey, I’d pay about £5-£7 for a whole book, so that’s fair! Then… you get about four chapters in, they start costing 7 points. Then 10 points. Then 15. Then 20. I’m almost certain it would have kept rising. And that’s PER chapter. And the chapters are not that long at all. That’s when you realise you’ve spent £5 on all those points and you’re not even a quarter of the way into the book. Or you can pay £50 for the whole year, unlimited reading. Now that might not be a bad option if you’re a serial reader and you want to spend all that cash in one go. But for those who just want to try out an entire book and see if that’ll whet their appetite for more of the same… it’s extortionate and extremely off putting. I stopped right there cold turkey; the book wasn’t THAT good that I’d be willing to spend £30 on it 🙄 So be careful if you’re paying per chapter.
